title: The blue line explains a day-of-the-following-month term
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: You start a new term due on a day of the following month and read the example the window gives.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Today's date on the calendar of {Location-A} is {Date-A}.
    For example: {Date-A} is Oct 21.
  • {Date-B} is the 10th of the month after {Date-A}.
    For example: {Date-B} is Nov 10.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Credit Term".
  2. Type "10th of next month" in Name.
  3. Click the Day box.
  4. Type 10 in the Day box.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the "New Credit Term" window opens.
  • Step 2: the Name reads 10th of next month.
  • Step 3: "Due day of the following month" is chosen.
  • Step 4: the blue line reads: "10th of next month means payment is due on the 10th of the following month. An invoice dated {Date-A} is due {Date-B}."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S3-R5: “While the chosen box holds a valid number, a blue information line below the options explains the term, using today's date as the example invoice date (S3-R16):”
  • S3-R5, day of the following month line: “Day of the following month: "{Name} means payment is due on the {ordinal X} of the following month. An invoice dated {today} is due {due}." For example: "10th of next month means payment is due on the 10th of the following month. An invoice dated Oct 21 is due Nov 10."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Valid day-of-month term typed | "{Name} means payment is due on the {ordinal X} of the following month. An invoice dated {today} is due {due}." | Blue information line, updates as the user types”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "3 New credit term and Inactive tab" ("New credit term: day of the following month"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes.

The design's own words:

  • “10th of next month means payment is due on the 10th of the following month. An invoice dated Oct 21 is due Nov 10.”
  • “The day field reads "of the following month" beside it. Always the next month, whatever the invoice day; a shorter month uses its last day.”
  • “Other messages: "Enter a name." and "Use 31 characters or fewer." Day: "Enter a day from 1 to 31." No sentence shows while a field is invalid.”
